ontology.note: Emits fw:PointBuffer with the source point, the radius as a QUDT quantity and the fraction of the true circle area the polygon covers. The output is fw:StudyArea: a derived scope is still a scope, and the derivation rather than the class is what distinguishes it from a surveyed boundary.

changes.description: Configure… offers the points the connected layer carries, by name, instead of asking for one to be typed against a placeholder. Where exactly one arrives the dialog opens on it, because one point is not a choice; where several do, the first entry says Choose a point and carries no value, so the control never reads as an answer the step does not hold. A point already chosen stays on the list even where the layer no longer offers it. A source that holds no records of its own and has not run offers nothing, and the name is typed in as before, with a line saying a run will populate it.

evidence.note: Five unit checks cover the circle approximation against the true area, naming a point by id or by name, the recorded source point and radius with its unit, refusal of blank, unknown and unlocated points, and the distance bound. The radius is an assumption of the question and no threshold is established as defensible; see docs/experiments/68-area-around-a-point.md. Composition is established by tests/composition-elevation.test.mjs, which wires this to Clip raster and Sample raster at points and shows that a tighter scope windows the grid, so an uncovered facility is reported as outside the raster rather than as no-data. 0.3.0: tests/buffer-point-inspector.browser.mjs (one point arriving is chosen and Apply records it; three are offered in the layer's order behind a Choose a point entry, with the refusal standing until one is picked; an empty source still asks for a name and says a run will populate it); Chromium, 2026-11-23.
